Each section runs one analysis twice over the same file: once with **`metacooler-run`** — the
Analysis panel from a shell, the same code the browser runs — and once with the **package the
analysis reproduces**, called the way that package is meant to be called and never re-implemented
here. The two outputs are then lined up bin by bin, or call by call, and the distance between them
is measured. Where the two definitions differ on purpose, the section says where, and measures the
agreement separately there.

| § | Analysis | Data (rsglab bucket) | Reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Diamond insulation | `demo/mouse/Murphy2023_TSC_HiC.mcool`, 10 kb | `cooltools.insulation` |
| 2 | Directionality index | the same map, 50 kb | `domaincaller` (Dixon et al. 2012's index) |
| 3 | Compartments | the same map, 100 kb | `cooltools.eigs_cis` |
| 4 | P(s) | `demo/yeast/Yeast_microC_G2M_1kb.cool`, and the mouse map at 10 kb | `cooltools.expected_cis` |
| 5 | Peak calling | `demo/yeast/Yeast_ATAC.bw` | yapc 0.1 |
| 6 | Loops | the yeast G2/M micro-C map, 1 kb | chromosight 1.6.3 |
| 7 | Reproducibility (HiCRep) | `demo/chicken`, seven 4DN DT40 maps, 100 kb | hicrep 0.2.6 and hicreppy 0.1.0 |
| 8 | 3D model (pastis-NB) | the yeast G2/M micro-C map, 10 kb | pastis, GitHub `6888ac2` |

Every reference runs as a command — its own command line where it has one, otherwise a short Python
script this notebook writes — and that command is what produces the result compared, what the
summary prints next to the `metacooler-run` command, and what the last section times, five times
each. Every command runs from `notebooks/work/validation/`, where the data are, and is printed with
its paths as it was given them.

**Before rendering.** `npm run build:cli` at the repository root, which builds this checkout's
`metacooler-run`. Then two Python environments:

```bash
# The notebook's own: the reference packages. pandas < 3 because chromosight 1.6.3
# writes its table with a call pandas 3's string dtype refuses.
python -m venv refs && . refs/bin/activate
pip install jupyter matplotlib cooler cooltools bioframe pyfaidx pyBigWig 'pandas<3' \
    chromosight==1.6.3 hicrep==0.2.6 hicreppy==0.1.0 domaincaller==0.1.0 \
    'git+https://github.com/hiclib/pastis@6888ac25ded72ce3e559987b8a31b3f8ed2935ed'
```

and yapc 0.1 in a venv of its own, because it installs only under numpy < 1.24 — the recipe is the
yapc section of `scripts/make_analysis_golden.py`, whose `yapc-env` this notebook runs as
`YAPC_PYTHON`. Then

```bash
QUARTO_PYTHON=refs/bin/python YAPC_PYTHON=yapc-env/bin/python \
    quarto render notebooks/validation.qmd
```

The data are fetched from the bucket once, into `notebooks/work/validation/data/` (about 7 GB, most
of it the chicken maps and the mm10 FASTA), and every command's outputs are kept beside them, so a
second render reads rather than recomputes (`REDO` below); the timings are kept the same way
(`REDO_BENCHMARK`). The first render takes about an hour, most of it the timing.

```{python}
from pathlib import Path
import os

#: Run a step again even where its outputs are already on disk.
REDO = False
#: How many times the last section times each command, and whether to time them again.
RUNS = 5
REDO_BENCHMARK = False
#: Processes for the reference packages that take them.
THREADS = 4
#: yapc 0.1's interpreter: a venv of its own (see above), relative to the repository or absolute.
YAPC_PYTHON = os.environ.get('YAPC_PYTHON', 'yapc-env/bin/python')

HERE = Path.cwd().resolve()
REPO = HERE.parent if HERE.name == 'notebooks' else HERE
CLI = REPO / 'dist-cli' / 'metacooler-run.mjs'
WORK = REPO / 'notebooks' / 'work' / 'validation'
DATA = WORK / 'data'
SCRIPTS = WORK / 'scripts'
BUCKET = 'https://rsglab-data.s3.eu-west-3.amazonaws.com'
YAPC_PYTHON = Path(YAPC_PYTHON) if Path(YAPC_PYTHON).is_absolute() else REPO / YAPC_PYTHON
```

```{python}
import html
import json
import platform
import re
import resource
import shlex
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import textwrap
import time
import urllib.request
import warnings
from importlib.metadata import version

import cooler
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap
from scipy import stats

warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
if not CLI.exists():
    raise FileNotFoundError(f'{CLI} is not there: run `npm run build:cli` at the repository root.')
DATA.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
SCRIPTS.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
PYTHON = sys.executable
CHROMOSIGHT = shutil.which('chromosight') or str(Path(PYTHON).parent / 'chromosight')
YAPC_ENV = dict(os.environ, PATH=f'{YAPC_PYTHON.parent}{os.pathsep}{os.environ["PATH"]}')


def fetch(key):
    """A file of the rsglab bucket, fetched once into work/validation/data."""
    path = DATA / Path(key).name
    if not path.exists():
        print('fetching', f'{BUCKET}/{key}')
        part = path.with_name(path.name + '.part')
        with urllib.request.urlopen(f'{BUCKET}/{key}') as response, open(part, 'wb') as out:
            shutil.copyfileobj(response, out, 1 << 22)
        part.rename(path)
    return path


def rel(path):
    """A path the way the commands give it: from work/validation/, where they run."""
    path = Path(path)
    return str(path.relative_to(WORK)) if path.is_relative_to(WORK) else str(path)


def arg(value):
    return rel(value) if isinstance(value, Path) else str(value)


def typed(argv):
    """A command as a reader would type it: each tool by its name, as it is installed."""
    names = {PYTHON: 'python', str(YAPC_PYTHON): 'yapc-env/bin/python', CHROMOSIGHT: 'chromosight'}
    if argv[:2] == ['node', str(CLI)]:
        argv = ['metacooler-run', *argv[2:]]
    return shlex.join([names.get(a, a) for a in argv])


#: Every metacooler-run command, and every reference command, by name: for the summary and the timing.
APP, REFS, NOTES = {}, {}, {}
#: Where a reference writes, in its command.
OUT = '<out>'


def mr(task, *args, out, name, analysis, label='', bench=True):
    """One metacooler-run command into `out`, skipped when `out` already holds its outputs.

    The command is printed, and the notes it prints are kept beside its outputs."""
    out = Path(out)
    argv = ['node', str(CLI), task, *[arg(a) for a in args]]
    full = argv + ['--out', rel(out)]
    APP[name] = dict(analysis=analysis, tool='metacooler-run', label=label, argv=argv, bench=bench,
                     shown=typed(full))
    print('$', typed(full))
    if not (out / '.command').exists() or REDO:
        out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        start = time.time()
        run = subprocess.run(full, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=WORK)
        if run.returncode:
            raise RuntimeError(run.stderr[-4000:])
        notes = [line.strip()[len('note: '):] for line in re.split(r'[\r\n]', run.stderr)
                 if line.strip().startswith('note:')]
        (out / '.notes').write_text('\n'.join(notes))
        (out / '.command').write_text(f'{typed(full)}\n# {time.time() - start:.1f} s\n')
    NOTES[name] = (out / '.notes').read_text().splitlines()
    return out


def script(name, text):
    """A reference's Python, written to work/validation/scripts/ to be run, printed and timed."""
    path = SCRIPTS / f'{name}.py'
    path.write_text(textwrap.dedent(text).strip().replace('__THREADS__', str(THREADS)) + '\n')
    return path


def reference(name, analysis, tool, argv, out, made=None, env=None, label='', bench=True):
    """A reference command, run once for the comparison (skipped when its output is on disk).

    `argv` holds OUT where the command writes, so the timing can send it elsewhere."""
    argv = [a if a == OUT else arg(a) for a in argv]
    out = Path(out)
    real = [rel(out) if a == OUT else a for a in argv]
    REFS[name] = dict(analysis=analysis, tool=tool, label=label, argv=argv, out=out, env=env, bench=bench,
                      shown=typed(real), scripts=[a for a in argv if a.endswith('.py')])
    print('$', typed(real))
    if REDO or not Path(made or out).exists():
        out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        run = subprocess.run(real, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=WORK, env=env)
        if run.returncode:
            raise RuntimeError(run.stderr[-4000:])
    return out


def table(path):
    """A table metacooler-run wrote: its '#' header lines are provenance, not data."""
    return pd.read_csv(path, sep='\t', comment='#')


def one(folder, pattern):
    """The one file of `folder` matching `pattern`."""
    hits = sorted(Path(folder).glob(pattern))
    if len(hits) != 1:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f'{len(hits)} files match {pattern} in {folder}')
    return hits[0]


def cached(path, compute):
    """A result of this notebook's own computed once and kept: a table as TSV, an array as NPY."""
    path = Path(path)
    if path.exists() and not REDO:
        return pd.read_csv(path, sep='\t') if path.suffix == '.tsv' else np.load(path)
    value = compute()
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if path.suffix == '.tsv':
        value.to_csv(path, sep='\t', index=False)
    else:
        np.save(path, value)
    return value


def show(frame, precision=4, **formats):
    """A table without its row numbers: the columns named in `formats` their way, the others to `precision`."""
    return frame.style.hide(axis='index').format(formats or None, precision=precision)


def measures(values):
    """Named numbers as a two-column table, each written the way it should be read."""
    return pd.DataFrame(list(values.items()), columns=['measure', 'value']).style.hide(axis='index')


def pearson(a, b):
    ok = np.isfinite(a) & np.isfinite(b)
    return stats.pearsonr(a[ok], b[ok])[0]


def spearman(a, b):
    ok = np.isfinite(a) & np.isfinite(b)
    return stats.spearmanr(a[ok], b[ok])[0]


# The figures: blue is always metacooler-run, orange the reference, aqua a second reference.
APP_COLOUR, REF, REF2 = '#2a78d6', '#eb6834', '#1baf7a'
INK, INK2, GRID, SURFACE, MISSING = '#0b0b0b', '#52514e', '#e7e6e2', '#fcfcfb', '#efeeea'
DENSITY = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list(
    'density', ['#cde2fb', '#86b6ef', '#3987e5', '#1c5cab', '#0d366b'])
plt.rcParams.update({
    'figure.facecolor': SURFACE, 'axes.facecolor': SURFACE, 'savefig.facecolor': SURFACE,
    'axes.edgecolor': INK2, 'axes.labelcolor': INK, 'xtick.color': INK2, 'ytick.color': INK2,
    'text.color': INK, 'axes.spines.top': False, 'axes.spines.right': False,
    'axes.grid': True, 'grid.color': GRID, 'grid.linewidth': 0.6, 'axes.axisbelow': True,
    'lines.linewidth': 2, 'font.size': 9, 'axes.titlesize': 10, 'axes.titleweight': 'bold',
    'axes.titlelocation': 'left', 'legend.frameon': False, 'figure.dpi': 110,
})


def identity(ax, lo, hi):
    ax.plot([lo, hi], [lo, hi], color=INK2, lw=1, ls=(0, (4, 3)), zorder=3)


def agreement(ax, x, y, xlabel, ylabel, title, scale='linear'):
    """Every pair of values as a density, against the identity line."""
    ok = np.isfinite(x) & np.isfinite(y)
    if scale == 'log':
        ok &= (x > 0) & (y > 0)
    x, y = x[ok], y[ok]
    ax.hexbin(x, y, gridsize=70, cmap=DENSITY, mincnt=1, bins='log', linewidths=0,
              xscale=scale, yscale=scale)
    identity(ax, min(x.min(), y.min()), max(x.max(), y.max()))
    ax.set_xlabel(xlabel)
    ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)
    ax.set_title(title)
    ax.text(0.03, 0.97, f'{ok.sum():,} values\nPearson r = {stats.pearsonr(x, y)[0]:.4f}',
            transform=ax.transAxes, va='top', fontsize=8, color=INK2)


TEXT = {}
SUMMARY = []


def commands(lines):
    return '<pre>' + html.escape('\n'.join(lines)) + '</pre>'


def record(task, data, reference_, agreement_, verdict, apps, refs):
    """One row of the summary, with the metacooler-run commands and the reference commands as they ran."""
    SUMMARY.append({'Analysis': task, 'Data': data,
                    'metacooler-run command': commands([f'$ {APP[name]["shown"]}' for name in apps]),
                    'Reference': reference_,
                    'Reference command': commands([f'$ {REFS[name]["shown"]}' for name in refs]),
                    'Agreement': agreement_, 'Verdict': verdict})
```

```{python}
def commit():
    run = subprocess.run(['git', 'rev-parse', '--short', 'HEAD'], capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=REPO)
    return run.stdout.strip() or 'unknown'


def yapc_versions():
    probe = 'import importlib.metadata as m; print(m.version("yapc"), m.version("idr"), m.version("numpy"))'
    try:
        run = subprocess.run([str(YAPC_PYTHON), '-c', probe], capture_output=True, text=True)
        return run.stdout.split() if run.returncode == 0 else ['?'] * 3
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return ['not found'] * 3


APP_VERSION = f"{json.loads((REPO / 'package.json').read_text())['version']} at {commit()}"
YAPC, IDR, YAPC_NUMPY = yapc_versions()
VERSIONS = {name: version(name) for name in (
    'cooler', 'cooltools', 'bioframe', 'chromosight', 'hicrep', 'hicreppy', 'domaincaller',
    'pastis', 'numpy', 'scipy', 'pandas')}
show(pd.DataFrame([{'package': 'metacooler-run', 'version': APP_VERSION},
                   *[{'package': k, 'version': v} for k, v in VERSIONS.items()],
                   {'package': 'yapc (own venv)', 'version': f'{YAPC}, with idr {IDR} and numpy {YAPC_NUMPY}'}]))
```

## 1 · Diamond insulation

**metacooler-run** `insulation`: for each bin, the contacts in a square of `window × window` bins
beside the diagonal, as a log2 ratio to the chromosome's mean; boundaries where the score has a
minimum at least `prominence` deep. **Reference:** `cooltools.insulation`, with the same window,
the same diagonals left out, the same floor on how much of the window must be present, and the same
boundary threshold.

| | metacooler-run | cooltools |
|---|---|---|
| window | `--window 10` (bins, 100 kb) | `window_bp=[100_000]` |
| diagonals left out | `--ignoreDiags 2` | `ignore_diags=2` |
| least share of the window present | `--minValid 0.5` | `min_frac_valid_pixels=0.5` |
| boundary threshold | `--prominence 0.2` | `threshold=0.2` |
| counts | balanced, the file's weights | `clr_weight_name='weight'` |

**The two are not one definition**, and `scripts/make_analysis_golden.py`, which holds this task to
cooltools in the unit tests, lists how. cooltools **averages** the valid pixels of a window whose rows
include the scored bin, and normalises by the chromosome's **median**; the app **sums** the pixels
present in a window that stops short of it, and normalises by the **mean**. Over a complete window a
sum is a mean times a constant, and either normalisation is one constant per chromosome, so the two
scores should follow each other there, half a bin apart. Where the window reaches a bin the balancer
dropped, a sum loses what is missing and a mean does not — so the comparison is split by whether the
window is complete.

```{python}
INS = WORK / 'insulation'
MOUSE_10K = f'{rel(MOUSE)}::/resolutions/10000'
mr('insulation', MOUSE_10K, '--window', 10, out=INS / 'app', name='insulation', analysis='Diamond insulation')
reference('cooltools-insulation', 'Diamond insulation', 'cooltools', [PYTHON, script('cooltools_insulation', r'''
    import sys, cooler, cooltools
    uri, out = sys.argv[1:]
    table = cooltools.insulation(cooler.Cooler(uri), [100_000], ignore_diags=2,
                                 clr_weight_name='weight', min_frac_valid_pixels=0.5,
                                 threshold=0.2, nproc=__THREADS__)
    table.to_csv(out, sep='\t', index=False)
'''), MOUSE_10K, OUT], out=INS / 'cooltools.tsv')

clr10 = cooler.Cooler(f'{MOUSE}::/resolutions/10000')
bins10 = clr10.bins()[:]
ref_ins = pd.read_csv(INS / 'cooltools.tsv', sep='\t')
app_ins = table(one(INS / 'app', '*.insulation-w10.tsv'))
# The app numbers its bins across the whole file, as cooler's bin table does.
assert (app_ins['bin'].to_numpy() == np.arange(len(bins10))).all()
a_ins = app_ins['value'].to_numpy(float)
b_ins = ref_ins['log2_insulation_score_100000'].to_numpy(float)


def complete_windows(bins, window):
    """Bins whose diamond lies wholly inside the chromosome and holds no dropped bin."""
    valid = np.isfinite(bins['weight'].to_numpy(float))
    out = np.zeros(len(bins), bool)
    for idx in bins.groupby('chrom', observed=True, sort=False).indices.values():
        v = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(valid[idx])])
        i = np.arange(len(idx))
        lo, hi = i - window, i + window + 1
        inside = (lo >= 0) & (hi <= len(idx))
        count = np.where(inside, v[np.clip(hi, 0, len(idx))] - v[np.clip(lo, 0, len(idx))], 0)
        out[idx] = inside & (count == 2 * window + 1)
    return out


complete = complete_windows(bins10, 10)
both = np.isfinite(a_ins) & np.isfinite(b_ins)
rows = []
for label, where in (('every bin both score', both), ('complete windows', both & complete),
                     ('windows touching a dropped bin', both & ~complete)):
    rows.append({'bins': label, 'n': int(where.sum()), 'Pearson r': pearson(a_ins[where], b_ins[where]),
                 'Spearman ρ': spearman(a_ins[where], b_ins[where])})
ins_table = pd.DataFrame(rows)
show(ins_table, n='{:,}')
```

```{python}
app_b = table(one(INS / 'app', '*.insulation-boundaries.tsv'))
ref_b = ref_ins.loc[ref_ins['is_boundary_100000'].astype(bool), ['chrom', 'start', 'boundary_strength_100000']]


def nearest(calls, others):
    """For each call, the distance to the nearest call of the other set on its chromosome."""
    out = np.full(len(calls), np.inf)
    for chrom, idx in calls.groupby('chrom', observed=True).indices.items():
        theirs = np.sort(others.loc[others['chrom'] == chrom, 'start'].to_numpy())
        if not len(theirs):
            continue
        mine = calls['start'].to_numpy()[idx]
        k = np.searchsorted(theirs, mine)
        left = np.abs(mine - theirs[np.clip(k - 1, 0, len(theirs) - 1)])
        right = np.abs(mine - theirs[np.clip(k, 0, len(theirs) - 1)])
        out[idx] = np.minimum(left, right)
    return out


rows = []
for label, mine, theirs in (
        ('every call', app_b, ref_b),
        ('calls at least 0.5 deep', app_b[app_b['score'] >= 0.5],
         ref_b[ref_b['boundary_strength_100000'] >= 0.5])):
    d_app, d_ref = nearest(mine.reset_index(drop=True), theirs), nearest(theirs.reset_index(drop=True), mine)
    row = {'boundaries': label, 'metacooler-run': len(mine), 'cooltools': len(theirs)}
    for bins_off in (0, 1, 2):
        row[f'≤ {bins_off} bin'] = f'{(d_app <= bins_off * 10_000).mean():.1%} · {(d_ref <= bins_off * 10_000).mean():.1%}'
    rows.append(row)
bnd_table = pd.DataFrame(rows)
show(bnd_table, **{'metacooler-run': '{:,}', 'cooltools': '{:,}'})
```

Each boundary cell reads *share of metacooler-run's calls with a cooltools call that near · share
of cooltools' calls with a metacooler-run call that near*.

```{python}
#| label: fig-insulation
#| fig-cap: "Diamond insulation, metacooler-run against cooltools, mouse Hi-C at 10 kb, 100 kb window. a, b, every bin both score, split by whether the window is complete; c, a stretch of chr11, dropped bins shaded."
r_all = ins_table['Pearson r']
TEXT['ins_all'] = f'{r_all[0]:.3f}'
TEXT['ins_complete'] = f'{r_all[1]:.3f}'
TEXT['ins_touching'] = f'{r_all[2]:.3f}'
TEXT['ins_share_touching'] = f'{(both & ~complete).sum() / both.sum():.0%}'
TEXT['ins_within1'] = bnd_table.loc[0, '≤ 1 bin'].split(' · ')[0]
TEXT['ins_strong_within1'] = bnd_table.loc[1, '≤ 1 bin'].split(' · ')[0]
TEXT['ins_exact'] = bnd_table.loc[0, '≤ 0 bin'].split(' · ')[0]

fig = plt.figure(figsize=(11, 7.2), layout='constrained')
grid = fig.add_gridspec(2, 2, height_ratios=[1.15, 1])
ax = fig.add_subplot(grid[0, 0])
agreement(ax, b_ins[both & complete], a_ins[both & complete], 'cooltools (log2)', 'metacooler-run (log2)',
          'a  complete windows')
ax = fig.add_subplot(grid[0, 1])
agreement(ax, b_ins[both & ~complete], a_ins[both & ~complete], 'cooltools (log2)', 'metacooler-run (log2)',
          'b  windows touching a dropped bin')
ax = fig.add_subplot(grid[1, :])
lo, hi = clr10.extent('chr11')
stretch = slice(lo + 3_000, lo + 4_000)
x = bins10['start'].to_numpy()[stretch] / 1e6
dropped = ~np.isfinite(bins10['weight'].to_numpy(float)[stretch])
for pos in x[dropped]:
    ax.axvspan(pos, pos + 0.01, color=MISSING, lw=0, zorder=0)
ax.plot(x, b_ins[stretch], color=REF, lw=2, label='cooltools')
ax.plot(x, a_ins[stretch], color=APP_COLOUR, lw=1.2, label='metacooler-run')
ax.set(xlabel='chr11 (Mb)', ylabel='insulation (log2)', title='c  chr11, 30–40 Mb')
ax.legend(loc='lower left', ncols=2)
plt.show()
```

**Over complete windows the two scores correlate at r = `{python} TEXT['ins_complete']`**, and over
every bin both score at `{python} TEXT['ins_all']`: the gap is the `{python} TEXT['ins_share_touching']`
of bins whose window reaches a dropped bin — many, on this map at 10 kb — where they correlate at only
`{python} TEXT['ins_touching']`, because one definition sums what is left and the other averages it.
Boundaries: `{python} TEXT['ins_within1']` of the app's calls have a cooltools call within one bin
(`{python} TEXT['ins_strong_within1']` of the calls at least 0.5 deep), and only
`{python} TEXT['ins_exact']` fall on the very same bin — which is what two windows half a bin apart
give. These are the differences the golden documents; the kernel itself (`diamondSums`) is held to
cooltools cell for cell in the unit tests.

```{python}
record('Diamond insulation', 'mouse Hi-C, 10 kb, window 100 kb', f"cooltools {VERSIONS['cooltools']}",
       f"r = {TEXT['ins_complete']} over complete windows ({TEXT['ins_all']} over all); "
       f"{TEXT['ins_within1']} of boundaries within 1 bin",
```

## 2 · Directionality index

**metacooler-run** `di`: Dixon et al. (2012)'s index — `A`, the contacts a bin makes upstream within
the window, `B` downstream, and `sign(B − A)·(B − A)²/(A + B)`. **Reference:** `domaincaller`, whose
`Chrom.calDI` computes it; it is called on the balanced matrix exactly as `domaincaller`'s own script
builds it. The script then fits its HMM for domains, which is not compared here.

| | metacooler-run | domaincaller |
|---|---|---|
| window | `--window 40` (bins, 2 Mb at 50 kb) | `calDI(window=2_000_000)` |
| cells | every cell off the diagonal, `--ignoreDiags 0` | the upper triangle off the diagonal |
| counts | balanced, the file's weights | `matrix(balance='weight')` |
| coverage | `--minValid 0.5`: no score where either side holds under half its window | a score everywhere |

The map has no 40 kb level, so this is Dixon's 2 Mb window at 50 kb.

```{python}
DI = WORK / 'di'
MOUSE_50K = f'{rel(MOUSE)}::/resolutions/50000'
mr('di', MOUSE_50K, '--window', 40, out=DI / 'app', name='di', analysis='Directionality index')
reference('domaincaller-di', 'Directionality index', 'domaincaller', [PYTHON, script('domaincaller_di', r'''
    import sys, cooler, numpy as np
    from domaincaller.chromLev import Chrom
    uri, out = sys.argv[1:]
    clr = cooler.Cooler(uri)
    di = np.full(clr.info['nbins'], np.nan)
    for chrom in clr.chromnames:
        # One chromosome, balanced and sparse, as domaincaller's own script builds it.
        matrix = clr.matrix(balance='weight', sparse=True).fetch(chrom).tocsr()
        work = Chrom(chrom, clr.binsize, matrix)
        work.calDI(window=2_000_000)
        lo = clr.extent(chrom)[0]
        di[lo:lo + len(work.DIs)] = work.DIs
    np.save(out, di)
'''), MOUSE_50K, OUT], out=DI / 'domaincaller.npy')

clr50 = cooler.Cooler(f'{MOUSE}::/resolutions/50000')
b_di = np.load(DI / 'domaincaller.npy')
a_di = table(one(DI / 'app', '*.di-w40.tsv'))['value'].to_numpy(float)
ok = np.isfinite(a_di) & np.isfinite(b_di)
floor = np.median(np.abs(b_di[ok]))
relative = np.abs(a_di[ok] - b_di[ok]) / np.maximum(np.abs(b_di[ok]), floor)
di_only_ref = int((np.isfinite(b_di) & ~np.isfinite(a_di)).sum())
measures({
    'bins both score': f'{ok.sum():,}',
    'bins only domaincaller scores': f'{di_only_ref:,}',
    'bins only metacooler-run scores': f'{int((np.isfinite(a_di) & ~np.isfinite(b_di)).sum()):,}',
    'Pearson r': f'{stats.pearsonr(a_di[ok], b_di[ok])[0]:.6f}',
    'relative difference, median': f'{np.median(relative):.1e}',
    'relative difference, max': f'{relative.max():.1e}',
    'same sign': f'{(np.sign(a_di[ok]) == np.sign(b_di[ok])).mean():.2%}',
})
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-di
#| fig-cap: "Directionality index, metacooler-run against domaincaller, mouse Hi-C at 50 kb, 2 Mb window. a, every bin both score (both axes symmetric-log); b, a stretch of chr2."
TEXT['di_max'] = f'{relative.max():.1e}'
TEXT['di_n'] = f'{ok.sum():,}'
TEXT['di_only_ref'] = f'{di_only_ref:,}'

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4.2), layout='constrained', width_ratios=[1, 1.6])
ax = axes[0]
ax.scatter(b_di[ok], a_di[ok], s=3, color=APP_COLOUR, alpha=0.35, lw=0, rasterized=True)
lim = np.abs(b_di[ok]).max()
identity(ax, -lim, lim)
TICKS = [-1, -0.1, -0.01, 0, 0.01, 0.1, 1]
ax.set_xscale('symlog', linthresh=0.01)
ax.set_yscale('symlog', linthresh=0.01)
ax.set_xticks(TICKS, [f'{t:g}' for t in TICKS])
ax.set_yticks(TICKS, [f'{t:g}' for t in TICKS])
ax.xaxis.set_minor_locator(plt.NullLocator())
ax.yaxis.set_minor_locator(plt.NullLocator())
ax.set(xlabel='domaincaller', ylabel='metacooler-run', title='a  every bin')
ax.text(0.03, 0.97, f"{ok.sum():,} bins\nmax relative difference {relative.max():.1e}",
        transform=ax.transAxes, va='top', fontsize=8, color=INK2)
ax = axes[1]
lo, _ = clr50.extent('chr2')
stretch = slice(lo + 800, lo + 1_400)
x = clr50.bins()['start'][:].to_numpy()[stretch] / 1e6
ax.plot(x, b_di[stretch], color=REF, lw=3, label='domaincaller')
ax.plot(x, a_di[stretch], color=APP_COLOUR, lw=1.2, label='metacooler-run')
ax.axhline(0, color=INK2, lw=0.8)
ax.set(xlabel='chr2 (Mb)', ylabel='directionality index', title='b  chr2, 40–70 Mb')
ax.legend(loc='lower left', ncols=2)

```

**The two are the same numbers**: over the `{python} TEXT['di_n']` bins both score, the largest
relative difference is `{python} TEXT['di_max']` — float32 rounding — and every sign agrees. The
`{python} TEXT['di_only_ref']` bins only domaincaller scores are the app's coverage rule: at a
chromosome's ends and beside gaps, one side of the window is mostly empty and the app leaves the bin
blank rather than reading a one-sided sum as a direction.

```{python}
       'Identical (float32)', apps=['di'], refs=['domaincaller-di'])
```

## 3 · Compartments

**metacooler-run** `compartments`, with its default preparation — cooltools': observed/expected cis,
clipped at its 99.9th percentile, less one, gaps as expected — and three eigenvectors, ranked by
eigenvalue and signed by GC content. **Reference:** `cooltools.eigs_cis`, signed by the same track.
The GC content is computed once, per 100 kb bin with `bioframe.frac_gc`, and handed to both, so a
difference in sign would be a difference in the method rather than in the phasing data; it is
input to both rather than part of either, so it is not timed.

| | metacooler-run | cooltools |
|---|---|---|
| components | `--components 3` | `n_eigs=3` |
| phasing | `--phaseTrack gc.bedGraph` | `phasing_track=gc` |
| diagonals left out | 2 (default) | `ignore_diags=2` |
| clipping | the 99.9th percentile (default) | `clip_percentile=99.9` |
| counts | balanced | `clr_weight_name='weight'` |

One difference is known: cooltools signs a component by its **Spearman** correlation with the
phasing track, the app by its **Pearson** correlation, and the app leaves the sign alone — and says
so — when that correlation is under 0.1. The two give the same sign unless the correlation is near
zero.

```{python}
CMP = WORK / 'compartments'
MOUSE_100K = f'{rel(MOUSE)}::/resolutions/100000'
clr100 = cooler.Cooler(f'{MOUSE}::/resolutions/100000')


def gc_content():
    import bioframe
    genome = bioframe.load_fasta(str(MM10), engine='pyfaidx')
    # The FASTA names its records 'mm10||chr1'; the map names them 'chr1'.
    genome = {name.split('||')[-1]: record for name, record in genome.items()}
    return bioframe.frac_gc(clr100.bins()[['chrom', 'start', 'end']][:], genome)


gc = cached(CMP / 'gc.tsv', gc_content)
GC_TRACK = CMP / 'gc.bedGraph'
if REDO or not GC_TRACK.exists():
    gc.dropna()[['chrom', 'start', 'end', 'GC']].to_csv(GC_TRACK, sep='\t', header=False, index=False)
mr('compartments', MOUSE_100K, '--components', 3, '--phaseTrack', GC_TRACK, out=CMP / 'app',
   name='compartments', analysis='Compartments')
reference('cooltools-eigs', 'Compartments', 'cooltools', [PYTHON, script('cooltools_eigs_cis', r'''
    import sys, cooler, cooltools, pandas as pd
    uri, gc, out = sys.argv[1:]
    values, vectors = cooltools.eigs_cis(
        cooler.Cooler(uri), phasing_track=pd.read_csv(gc, sep='\t'), n_eigs=3,
        clr_weight_name='weight', ignore_diags=2, clip_percentile=99.9)
    values.to_csv(f'{out}-eigenvalues.tsv', sep='\t', index=False)
    vectors.to_csv(f'{out}-eigenvectors.tsv', sep='\t', index=False)
'''), MOUSE_100K, CMP / 'gc.tsv', OUT], out=CMP / 'cooltools', made=CMP / 'cooltools-eigenvectors.tsv')

ref_vec = pd.read_csv(CMP / 'cooltools-eigenvectors.tsv', sep='\t')
ref_val = pd.read_csv(CMP / 'cooltools-eigenvalues.tsv', sep='\t')
app_vec = {k: table(one(CMP / 'app', f'*.compartment-e{k}.tsv'))['value'].to_numpy(float) for k in (1, 2, 3)}
app_comp = table(one(CMP / 'app', '*.compartment-components.tsv'))


def first(values):
    return values.iloc[0] if len(values) else np.nan


rows = []
chrom100 = ref_vec['chrom'].astype(str).to_numpy()
for chrom in clr100.chromnames:
    s = chrom100 == chrom
    row = {'chromosome': chrom}
    for k in (1, 2, 3):
        mine, theirs = app_vec[k][s], ref_vec[f'E{k}'].to_numpy(float)[s]
        row[f'r E{k}'] = pearson(mine, theirs)
        eig_app = first(app_comp.loc[(app_comp['sequence'] == chrom) & (app_comp['component'] == f'E{k}'), 'eigenvalue'])
        eig_ref = first(ref_val.loc[ref_val['name'] == chrom, f'eigval{k}'])
        row[f'eigenvalue E{k}, relative difference'] = abs(eig_app / eig_ref - 1)
    e1a, e1b = app_vec[1][s], ref_vec['E1'].to_numpy(float)[s]
    ok = np.isfinite(e1a) & np.isfinite(e1b)
    row['A/B agreement'] = (np.sign(e1a[ok]) == np.sign(e1b[ok])).mean()
    phase = first(app_comp.loc[(app_comp['sequence'] == chrom) & (app_comp['component'] == 'E1'), 'r'])
    row['E1 against GC (app)'] = phase
    row['phasing'] = 'set' if abs(phase) >= 0.1 else 'ambiguous'
    rows.append(row)
cmp_table = pd.DataFrame(rows)
show(cmp_table)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-compartments
#| fig-cap: "Compartments, metacooler-run against cooltools.eigs_cis, mouse Hi-C at 100 kb, both signed by GC content. a, the correlation between the two tools' components, chromosome by chromosome; b, E1 along chr1."
phased = cmp_table[cmp_table['phasing'] == 'set']
TEXT['cmp_min_r'] = f"{phased['r E1'].min():.4f}"
TEXT['cmp_median_r'] = f"{phased['r E1'].median():.5f}"
TEXT['cmp_n'] = f'{len(phased)}'
TEXT['cmp_eig'] = f"{phased['eigenvalue E1, relative difference'].max():.2%}"
TEXT['cmp_ab'] = f"{phased['A/B agreement'].min():.2%}"
TEXT['cmp_ambiguous'] = ', '.join(cmp_table.loc[cmp_table['phasing'] == 'ambiguous', 'chromosome']) or 'none'
e23 = pd.DataFrame([{'component': f'E{k}', 'chromosome': row['chromosome'], 'r': row[f'r E{k}'],
                     'eigenvalue': row[f'eigenvalue E{k}, relative difference']}
                    for k in (2, 3) for _, row in phased.iterrows()])
alike = e23['r'].abs() >= 0.98
odd = e23[~alike]
twins = odd[odd['eigenvalue'] > 1.5]
mixed = odd[odd['eigenvalue'] <= 1.5]


def listed(items):
    items = list(items)
    return items[0] if len(items) == 1 else ', '.join(items[:-1]) + ' and ' + items[-1]


sentence = (f"E2 and E3 are the same vectors up to sign on {alike.sum()} of the {len(e23)} chromosome-components "
            f"(|r| ≥ 0.98), {(e23['r'] <= -0.98).sum()} of them with the opposite sign: E2 and E3 barely follow GC "
            f"content, so the sign each tool gives them is arbitrary.")
if len(twins):
    sentence += (' ' + listed(f'{r.component} on {r.chromosome}' for r in twins.itertuples()) +
                 (' is a tie' if len(twins) == 1 else ' are ties') +
                 ': the eigenvalue ranked third has a twin of the opposite sign and almost the same magnitude — '
                 'the eigenvalue column reads 2.0, one tool\'s +λ against the other\'s −λ — and, ranked by |λ|, '
                 'each tool took a different one of the pair.')
if len(mixed):
    sentence += (' ' + listed(f'{r.component} on {r.chromosome} (|r| = {abs(r.r):.2f})' for r in mixed.itertuples()) +
                 (' sits' if len(mixed) == 1 else ' sit') +
                 ' beside an eigenvalue of nearly the same size, where any mixture of the two is an equally good '
                 'eigenvector.')
TEXT['cmp_e23_sentence'] = sentence

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4.2), layout='constrained', width_ratios=[1.25, 1])
ax = axes[0]
x = np.arange(len(cmp_table))
for k, colour, offset in ((1, APP_COLOUR, -0.2), (2, REF, 0), (3, REF2, 0.2)):
    ax.scatter(x + offset, cmp_table[f'r E{k}'].abs(), s=24, color=colour, label=f'E{k}', zorder=3)
ax.set_xticks(x, cmp_table['chromosome'].str.replace('chr', ''), fontsize=7)
ax.set(ylim=(0, 1.05), xlabel='chromosome', ylabel='|Pearson r|, metacooler-run vs cooltools',
       title='a  each component, each chromosome')
ax.legend(loc='lower left', ncols=3)
ax = axes[1]
s = chrom100 == 'chr1'
xs = ref_vec['start'].to_numpy()[s] / 1e6
ax.plot(xs, ref_vec['E1'].to_numpy(float)[s], color=REF, lw=3, label='cooltools')
ax.plot(xs, app_vec[1][s], color=APP_COLOUR, lw=1.2, label='metacooler-run')
ax.axhline(0, color=INK2, lw=0.8)
ax.set(xlabel='chr1 (Mb)', ylabel='E1', title='b  E1 along chr1')
ax.legend(loc='lower left', ncols=2)
plt.show()
```

**E1 is the same vector**: on every one of the `{python} TEXT['cmp_n']` chromosomes whose phasing the
app could set, the two E1 correlate at r ≥ `{python} TEXT['cmp_min_r']` (median
`{python} TEXT['cmp_median_r']`), their eigenvalues agree within `{python} TEXT['cmp_eig']`, and the
A/B call agrees on at least `{python} TEXT['cmp_ab']` of each chromosome's bins. The one exception is
`{python} TEXT['cmp_ambiguous']`, mostly unmappable at this resolution, where the app reports its
phasing as ambiguous and says E1's sign should not be compared with another run — which is what
the negative correlation in the table is. `{python} TEXT['cmp_e23_sentence']`

```{python}
record('Compartments', 'mouse Hi-C, 100 kb, GC-phased', f"cooltools {VERSIONS['cooltools']}",
       f"E1 r ≥ {TEXT['cmp_min_r']} on {TEXT['cmp_n']} chromosomes; eigenvalues within {TEXT['cmp_eig']}; "
```

## 4 · P(s)

**metacooler-run** `expected` with `--quantity expected --scope file`: over the whole map, bands of
separations spaced by a factor of 1.1, and in each band the balanced contacts summed over every
chromosome divided by the number of bin pairs that could have held one — reported at the band's mean
separation, weighted by those pairs. **Reference:** `cooltools.expected_cis`, one row per chromosome
and diagonal, with the balanced sum and the number of valid pixels. cooltools' own `logbin_expected`
pools those rows exactly this way — sums over a band of diagonals, then one division — only over its
own bands, ten per decade. So the per-diagonal sums are pooled here over **the app's bands**: each is
a run of consecutive diagonals whose weighted mean is the separation the app wrote, so the runs can be
read off left to right. Every point of the curve is then compared with its exact counterpart.

The app's **default** quantity is another one: `density`, HiContacts' `distanceLaw` share of all cis
contacts per base pair, which the unit tests hold to HiContacts itself in R (`hicontacts_ps`). R is
not part of this notebook's environment, so that form is not re-checked here.

```{python}
PS = WORK / 'ps'
PS_CASES = {'yeast micro-C, 1 kb': ('yeast', rel(YEAST_G2M), str(YEAST_G2M), 'yeast 1 kb'),
            'mouse Hi-C, 10 kb': ('mouse', MOUSE_10K, f'{MOUSE}::/resolutions/10000', 'mouse 10 kb')}
EXPECTED = script('cooltools_expected_cis', r'''
    import sys, cooler, cooltools
    uri, out = sys.argv[1:]
    table = cooltools.expected_cis(cooler.Cooler(uri), ignore_diags=0, smooth=False,
                                   aggregate_smoothed=False, clr_weight_name='weight',
                                   nproc=__THREADS__)
    table.to_csv(out, sep='\t', index=False)
''')


def bands(n_valid, separations, binsize):
    """The run of consecutive diagonals behind each separation the app wrote.

    A band's separation is the valid-pixel-weighted mean of its diagonals, written to six
    significant digits; each run is the longest one, from where the last ended, whose mean matches.
    Trailing diagonals with no valid pixel leave the mean where it is and belong to no one's value."""
    k = np.arange(len(n_valid), dtype=float)
    cn = np.concatenate([[0.0], np.cumsum(n_valid)])
    ck = np.concatenate([[0.0], np.cumsum(n_valid * k)])
    runs, lo = [], 1
    for x in separations:
        tolerance = max(0.5, abs(x) * 5e-6)
        match = None
        for hi in range(lo + 1, len(n_valid) + 1):
            w = cn[hi] - cn[lo]
            if w <= 0:
                continue
            mean = (ck[hi] - ck[lo]) / w * binsize
            if abs(mean - x) <= tolerance:
                match = hi
            elif mean > x + tolerance:
                break
        if match is None:
            raise ValueError(f'no run of diagonals from {lo} has its mean at {x}')
        runs.append((lo, match))
        lo = match
    return runs


ps = {}
for label, (slug, uri, local, short) in PS_CASES.items():
    mr('expected', uri, '--quantity', 'expected', '--scope', 'file', out=PS / slug, name=f'expected-{slug}',
       analysis='P(s)', label=short)
    reference(f'cooltools-expected-{slug}', 'P(s)', 'cooltools', [PYTHON, EXPECTED, uri, OUT],
              out=PS / f'{slug}-cooltools.tsv', label=short)
    app = table(one(PS / slug, '*.expected.ps.tsv'))
    cvd = pd.read_csv(PS / f'{slug}-cooltools.tsv', sep='\t')
    cvd['balanced.sum'] = cvd['balanced.sum'].fillna(0)
    ref = cvd.groupby('dist')[['n_valid', 'balanced.sum']].sum()
    n = ref['n_valid'].reindex(range(int(ref.index.max()) + 1), fill_value=0).to_numpy(float)
    total = ref['balanced.sum'].reindex(range(len(n)), fill_value=0).to_numpy(float)
    x, y = app.iloc[:, 0].to_numpy(float), app.iloc[:, 1].to_numpy(float)
    runs = bands(n, x, cooler.Cooler(local).binsize)
    pooled = np.array([total[a:b].sum() / n[a:b].sum() for a, b in runs])
    ps[label] = dict(x=x, app=y, ref=pooled, rel=np.abs(y / pooled - 1),
                     widest=max(b - a for a, b in runs), reach=x.max())
show(pd.DataFrame([{'map': k, 'points': len(v['x']), 'furthest separation (Mb)': v['reach'] / 1e6,
                    'widest band (diagonals)': v['widest'], 'relative difference, median': np.median(v['rel']),
                    'relative difference, max': v['rel'].max()} for k, v in ps.items()]),
     **{'furthest separation (Mb)': '{:.1f}', 'widest band (diagonals)': '{:,}',
        'relative difference, median': '{:.1e}', 'relative difference, max': '{:.1e}'})
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-ps
#| fig-cap: "P(s), metacooler-run against cooltools.expected_cis pooled over the same bands. Top, the curves; bottom, the relative difference at every point."
TEXT['ps_max'] = f"{max(v['rel'].max() for v in ps.values()):.1e}"
TEXT['ps_points'] = f"{sum(len(v['x']) for v in ps.values())}"

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(11, 6.4), layout='constrained', height_ratios=[1.4, 1], sharex='col')
for col, (label, v) in enumerate(ps.items()):
    ax = axes[0, col]
    ax.plot(v['x'], v['ref'], color=REF, lw=3, label='cooltools, pooled')
    ax.scatter(v['x'], v['app'], s=14, color=APP_COLOUR, zorder=3, label='metacooler-run')
    ax.set(xscale='log', yscale='log', ylabel='mean balanced contact per bin pair', title=label)
    ax.legend(loc='lower left')
    ax = axes[1, col]
    ax.scatter(v['x'], np.maximum(v['rel'], 1e-9), s=10, color=APP_COLOUR)
    ax.set(xscale='log', yscale='log', ylim=(1e-9, 1e-3), xlabel='separation (bp)',
           ylabel='|metacooler-run / cooltools − 1|')
plt.show()
```

**Every point is the same number**: across `{python} TEXT['ps_points']` points on the two maps, from
one bin of separation to the length of the longest chromosome, the largest relative difference is
`{python} TEXT['ps_max']` — the float32 the app sums in.

```{python}
record('P(s)', 'yeast micro-C 1 kb; mouse Hi-C 10 kb', f"cooltools {VERSIONS['cooltools']}",
       f"max relative difference {TEXT['ps_max']} over {TEXT['ps_points']} points",
       'Identical (float32)', apps=['expected-yeast', 'expected-mouse'],
       refs=['cooltools-expected-yeast', 'cooltools-expected-mouse'])
```

## 5 · Peak calling (yapc)

**metacooler-run** `peaks`: the app's port of yapc (Jänes et al. 2018) on a coverage track. The
bucket holds one ATAC-seq track, and with one track yapc's pipeline stops before its reproducibility
test (IDR needs two replicates), so what is compared is its **candidate stage**: the regions where
the smoothed signal's second derivative is negative, each with its summit and its score. **Reference:**
yapc 0.1 — the release on bioconda — its `bin/yapc` loaded with `runpy` and its own `coverage`,
`d2smooth`, `find_concave_regions` and `scores` called in order, as
`scripts/make_analysis_golden.py` calls them, in yapc's own environment. yapc's `main()` then keeps
the regions at least 75 bp wide, which is the one line applied here to its table.

| | metacooler-run | yapc 0.1 |
|---|---|---|
| smoothing | `--width 150 --times 3` | `prepare_second_derivative_kernel(150, 3)` |
| narrowest region | `--minWidth 75` | `main()`'s `concave_end − concave_start >= 75` |
| output | `--perPeak true`: every region | the candidate table |

The app's peak **table** counts from 1, as its tables do; its BED counts from 0, as yapc does.

```{python}
YP = WORK / 'yapc'
mr('peaks', '--signal', YEAST_ATAC, '--perPeak', 'true', '--width', 150, '--times', 3, '--minWidth', 75,
   out=YP / 'app', name='peaks', analysis='Peak calling (yapc)')
reference('yapc', 'Peak calling (yapc)', 'yapc 0.1', [YAPC_PYTHON, script('yapc_candidates', r'''
    """yapc 0.1's candidate stage on one bigWig: yapc's own functions, from bin/yapc."""
    import contextlib, io, os, runpy, shutil, sys, tempfile
    track, out = sys.argv[1:3]
    width, times = int(sys.argv[3]), int(sys.argv[4])
    ns = runpy.run_path(shutil.which('yapc'), run_name='yapc_reference')
    kernel = ns['prepare_second_derivative_kernel'](width, times)
    quiet = contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO())
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp, quiet:
        prefix = os.path.join(tmp, 'yapc')
        ns['coverage']([track], prefix + '_coverage.bw')
        ns['d2smooth'](prefix + '_coverage.bw', prefix + '_d2smooth.bw', kernel)
        regions = ns['find_concave_regions'](prefix + '_d2smooth.bw', None, None)
        regions['score'] = list(ns['scores'](
            track, regions.chrom.tolist(), regions.concave_start.tolist(),
            regions.concave_end.tolist(), kernel))
    columns = ['chrom', 'concave_start', 'concave_end', 'mode', 'score']
    regions[columns].to_csv(out, sep='\t', index=False)
'''), YEAST_ATAC, OUT, 150, 3], out=YP / 'yapc-candidates.tsv', env=YAPC_ENV)

ref_all = pd.read_csv(YP / 'yapc-candidates.tsv', sep='\t')
ref_peaks = ref_all[(ref_all['concave_end'] - ref_all['concave_start']) >= 75]
listing = table(one(YP / 'app', '*.peaks-list.tsv'))
bed = pd.read_csv(one(YP / 'app', '*.bed'), sep='\t', header=None, names=['chrom', 'start', 'end', 'name', 'score', 'strand'])
app_peaks = (listing.assign(start=listing['start'] - 1, summit=listing['summit'] - 1)
             .rename(columns={'sequence': 'chrom'})[['chrom', 'start', 'end', 'summit']]
             .merge(bed[['chrom', 'start', 'end', 'score']], on=['chrom', 'start', 'end'], how='left'))
m = app_peaks.merge(ref_peaks, left_on=['chrom', 'start', 'end'], right_on=['chrom', 'concave_start', 'concave_end'],
                    how='outer', indicator=True, suffixes=('_app', '_yapc'))
shared = m[m['_merge'] == 'both']
rel_score = np.abs(shared['score_app'] / shared['score_yapc'] - 1)
candidates_app = next((int(re.sub(r'\D', '', n.split(' concave')[0])) for n in NOTES['peaks'] if 'concave regions' in n), None)
measures({
    'concave regions, metacooler-run': f'{candidates_app:,}', 'concave regions, yapc': f'{len(ref_all):,}',
    'at least 75 bp, metacooler-run': f'{len(app_peaks):,}', 'at least 75 bp, yapc': f'{len(ref_peaks):,}',
    'same bounds': f'{len(shared):,}', 'only metacooler-run': f"{int((m['_merge'] == 'left_only').sum()):,}",
    'only yapc': f"{int((m['_merge'] == 'right_only').sum()):,}",
    'same summit': f"{(shared['summit'] == shared['mode']).mean():.2%}",
    'score, max relative difference': f'{rel_score.max():.1e}',
    'score ranks, Spearman ρ': f"{stats.spearmanr(shared['score_app'], shared['score_yapc'])[0]:.6f}",
})
```

## 6 · Loops (chromosight)

**metacooler-run** `chromosight --pattern loops`, with chromosight's own thresholds for loops — the
app's presets are chromosight's `kernels/loops.json`: 20 kb to 2 Mb from the diagonal, a Pearson
score of at least 0.3, one iteration, the same limits on empty and undetectable pixels.
**Reference:** `chromosight detect --pattern loops`, which reads the same preset. The two are
compared call for call, and the p- and q-values the app prints in each call's detail against the ones
chromosight writes.

```{python}
LP = WORK / 'loops'
mr('chromosight', YEAST_G2M, '--pattern', 'loops', out=LP / 'app', name='chromosight', analysis='Loops (chromosight)')
reference('chromosight', 'Loops (chromosight)', 'chromosight',
          [CHROMOSIGHT, 'detect', '--pattern', 'loops', '--threads', THREADS, YEAST_G2M, OUT],
          out=LP / 'chromosight' / 'loops', made=LP / 'chromosight' / 'loops.tsv')

ref_loops = pd.read_csv(LP / 'chromosight' / 'loops.tsv', sep='\t')
app_loops = table(one(LP / 'app', '*.chromosight-patterns.tsv'))
for key in ('p', 'q'):
    app_loops[key] = app_loops['detail'].str.extract(rf'\b{key} ([0-9.e+-]+)')[0].astype(float)
key = ['chrom1', 'start1', 'chrom2', 'start2']
m = app_loops.merge(ref_loops, on=key, how='outer', indicator=True, suffixes=('_app', '_ref'))
shared = m[m['_merge'] == 'both']
# chromosight writes p and q to ten decimals: compared where that leaves four significant digits.
readable = shared[shared['pvalue'] >= 1e-6]
readable_q = shared[shared['qvalue'] >= 1e-6]
measures({
    'loops, metacooler-run': f'{len(app_loops):,}', 'loops, chromosight': f'{len(ref_loops):,}',
    'same bin pair': f'{len(shared):,}', 'only metacooler-run': f"{int((m['_merge'] == 'left_only').sum()):,}",
    'only chromosight': f"{int((m['_merge'] == 'right_only').sum()):,}",
    'score, max difference': f"{np.abs(shared['score_app'] - shared['score_ref']).max():.1e}",
    f'p, max relative difference ({len(readable):,} loops with p ≥ 1e-6)':
        f"{np.abs(readable['p'] / readable['pvalue'] - 1).max():.1e}",
    f'q, max relative difference ({len(readable_q):,} loops with q ≥ 1e-6)':
        f"{np.abs(readable_q['q'] / readable_q['qvalue'] - 1).max():.1e}",
})
```

## 7 · Reproducibility (HiCRep)

**metacooler-run** `hicrep`: HiCRep's stratum-adjusted correlation (Yang et al. 2017) — both maps
smoothed with a 2D mean filter of half-width `h`, a Pearson correlation on each diagonal, and the
diagonals pooled with Cochran–Mantel–Haenszel weights. **References:** two published Python
implementations, `hicrep` (Lin) and `hicreppy`, which differ between themselves in details — hicrep
leaves the main diagonal out and drops the positions where both maps are zero; hicreppy keeps both —
so the app is compared with each, and the two with each other, which is the yardstick.

| | metacooler-run | hicrep | hicreppy |
|---|---|---|---|
| counts | raw, `--no-balance` | raw (`balance=False`) | raw (`balance=False`) |
| smoothing | `--smooth 1` | `h=1` | `h=1` |
| furthest diagonal | `--maxDistance 50` (5 Mb) | `dBPMax=5_000_000` | `max_dist=5_100_000` (diagonals 0–50) |
| depth | as read | `bDownSample=False` | no subsampling |

Seven maps of the chicken DT40 series in `demo/chicken` — G2, 5, 10, 15, 30 and 60 min, and
unsorted, as the files name them — every pair of them, over every chromosome long enough for all
three tools (hicreppy leaves out a chromosome shorter than the furthest separation).

```{python}
HR = WORK / 'hicrep'
RES, STRATA, H = 100_000, 50, 1
LABELS = list(CHICKEN)
URIS = {label: f'{rel(CHICKEN[label])}::/resolutions/{RES}' for label in LABELS}
first_map = cooler.Cooler(f'{CHICKEN[LABELS[0]]}::/resolutions/{RES}')
SEQS = [c for c, length in first_map.chromsizes.items() if length >= (STRATA + 1) * RES]
against = [a for label in LABELS[1:] for a in ('--against', URIS[label])]
mr('hicrep', URIS[LABELS[0]], *against, '--maxDistance', STRATA, '--smooth', H, '--no-balance',
   '--sequences', ','.join(SEQS), out=HR / 'app', name='hicrep', analysis='Reproducibility (HiCRep)',
   label='7 maps, 21 pairs')
MAPS = [f'{label}={URIS[label]}' for label in LABELS]
reference('hicrep', 'Reproducibility (HiCRep)', 'hicrep', [PYTHON, script('hicrep_scc', r'''
    import sys, cooler, pandas as pd
    from hicrep import hicrepSCC
    out, seqs = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2].split(',')
    maps = dict(m.split('=', 1) for m in sys.argv[3:])
    labels, rows = list(maps), []
    for i, a in enumerate(labels):
        for b in labels[i + 1:]:
            scc = hicrepSCC(cooler.Cooler(maps[a]), cooler.Cooler(maps[b]), h=1,
                            dBPMax=5_000_000, bDownSample=False, chrNames=seqs)
            rows += [dict(a=a, b=b, sequence=s, hicrep=v) for s, v in zip(seqs, scc)]
    pd.DataFrame(rows).to_csv(out, sep='\t', index=False)
'''), OUT, ','.join(SEQS), *MAPS], out=HR / 'hicrep.tsv', label='7 maps, 21 pairs')
reference('hicreppy', 'Reproducibility (HiCRep)', 'hicreppy', [PYTHON, script('hicreppy_scc', r'''
    import sys, cooler, pandas as pd
    from hicreppy.hicrep import genome_scc
    out, seqs = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2].split(',')
    maps = dict(m.split('=', 1) for m in sys.argv[3:])
    labels, rows = list(maps), []
    for i, a in enumerate(labels):
        for b in labels[i + 1:]:
            ca, cb = cooler.Cooler(maps[a]), cooler.Cooler(maps[b])
            for s in seqs:
                scc = genome_scc(ca, cb, max_dist=5_100_000, h=1, whitelist=[s])
                rows.append(dict(a=a, b=b, sequence=s, hicreppy=scc))
    pd.DataFrame(rows).to_csv(out, sep='\t', index=False)
'''), OUT, ','.join(SEQS), *MAPS], out=HR / 'hicreppy.tsv', label='7 maps, 21 pairs')

names = {'This map': LABELS[0], **{CHICKEN[label].name: label for label in LABELS}}
app_scc = table(one(HR / 'app', '*.hicrep-sequences.tsv'))
app_scc['a'], app_scc['b'] = app_scc['a'].map(names), app_scc['b'].map(names)


def unordered(frame):
    order = {label: i for i, label in enumerate(LABELS)}
    swap = frame['a'].map(order) > frame['b'].map(order)
    frame.loc[swap, ['a', 'b']] = frame.loc[swap, ['b', 'a']].to_numpy()
    return frame


scc = (unordered(app_scc[['a', 'b', 'sequence', 'scc']].rename(columns={'scc': 'metacooler-run'}))
       .merge(unordered(pd.read_csv(HR / 'hicrep.tsv', sep='\t')), on=['a', 'b', 'sequence'])
       .merge(unordered(pd.read_csv(HR / 'hicreppy.tsv', sep='\t')), on=['a', 'b', 'sequence']))
rows = []
for x, y in (('metacooler-run', 'hicrep'), ('metacooler-run', 'hicreppy'), ('hicrep', 'hicreppy')):
    d = scc[x] - scc[y]
    rows.append({'comparison': f'{x} − {y}', 'pairs × chromosomes': len(scc), 'mean difference': d.mean(),
                 'max |difference|': d.abs().max(), 'Pearson r': pearson(scc[x].to_numpy(), scc[y].to_numpy())})
scc_table = pd.DataFrame(rows)
show(scc_table, precision=3)
```

The app's SCC sits well above both references, which agree with each other. The per-diagonal
correlations show where: the same two maps on chr1, the app's own table of correlation by separation
against the per-diagonal correlation of the same matrices smoothed by hicreppy's own `smooth` —
`hicreppy.get_scc`'s first step for each diagonal, `pearsonr(mat1.diagonal(d), mat2.diagonal(d))`.

```{python}
import hicreppy.utils.mat_process as cu

PAIR = ('G2', '60m')
mr('hicrep', URIS[PAIR[0]], '--against', URIS[PAIR[1]], '--maxDistance', STRATA, '--smooth', H, '--no-balance',
   '--sequences', 'chr1', out=HR / 'app-chr1', name='hicrep-chr1', analysis='Reproducibility (HiCRep)',
   label='chr1, G2 vs 60m', bench=False)
strata_app = table(one(HR / 'app-chr1', '*.hicrep-strata.tsv')).iloc[:, 1].to_numpy(float)


def smoothed(label):
    raw = cooler.Cooler(f'{CHICKEN[label]}::/resolutions/{RES}').matrix(sparse=True, balance=False).fetch('chr1')
    return cu.smooth(cu.diag_trim(raw.todia(), STRATA + 1 + H).tocoo(), H).tocsr()


s1, s2 = smoothed(PAIR[0]), smoothed(PAIR[1])
strata_ref = np.array([stats.pearsonr(s1.diagonal(d), s2.diagonal(d))[0] for d in range(len(strata_app))])
pooled = scc[(scc['a'] == PAIR[0]) & (scc['b'] == PAIR[1]) & (scc['sequence'] == 'chr1')].iloc[0]
measures({'per-diagonal r, Pearson r between the two curves': f'{stats.pearsonr(strata_app, strata_ref)[0]:.5f}',
          'per-diagonal r, max |difference|': f'{np.abs(strata_app - strata_ref).max():.4f}',
          'plain mean of the per-diagonal r': f'{strata_app.mean():.3f}',
          'SCC, metacooler-run': f"{pooled['metacooler-run']:.3f}", 'SCC, hicrep': f"{pooled['hicrep']:.3f}",
          'SCC, hicreppy': f"{pooled['hicreppy']:.3f}"})
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-hicrep
#| fig-cap: "HiCRep on seven chicken DT40 maps, every pair, every chromosome of at least 5.1 Mb, at 100 kb. a–c, each implementation against the others; d, chr1 of G2 against 60 min: the correlation of each diagonal, and the SCC each tool pools them into."
TEXT['hr_app_lin'] = f"{scc_table.loc[0, 'mean difference']:+.2f}"
TEXT['hr_app_py'] = f"{scc_table.loc[1, 'mean difference']:+.2f}"
TEXT['hr_lin_py'] = f"{scc_table.loc[2, 'mean difference']:+.2f}"
TEXT['hr_lin_py_max'] = f"{scc_table.loc[2, 'max |difference|']:.2f}"
TEXT['hr_lin_py_r'] = f"{scc_table.loc[2, 'Pearson r']:.2f}"
TEXT['hr_app_r'] = f"{max(scc_table.loc[0, 'Pearson r'], scc_table.loc[1, 'Pearson r']):.2f}"
TEXT['hr_n'] = f'{len(scc)}'
TEXT['hr_strata_r'] = f"{stats.pearsonr(strata_app, strata_ref)[0]:.4f}"
TEXT['hr_chr1_app'] = f"{pooled['metacooler-run']:.2f}"
TEXT['hr_chr1_refs'] = f"{pooled['hicrep']:.2f} and {pooled['hicreppy']:.2f}"
TEXT['hr_chr1_mean'] = f'{strata_app.mean():.2f}'

fig = plt.figure(figsize=(11, 7.6), layout='constrained')
grid = fig.add_gridspec(2, 3, height_ratios=[1, 1.1])
for col, (x, y, title) in enumerate((('hicrep', 'metacooler-run', 'a'), ('hicreppy', 'metacooler-run', 'b'),
                                     ('hicrep', 'hicreppy', 'c'))):
    ax = fig.add_subplot(grid[0, col])
    ax.scatter(scc[x], scc[y], s=7, color=APP_COLOUR if y == 'metacooler-run' else REF2, alpha=0.5, lw=0)
    identity(ax, 0, 1)
    ax.set(xlim=(0, 1), ylim=(0, 1), xlabel=f'{x} SCC', ylabel=f'{y} SCC', title=f'{title}  {y} vs {x}')
    ax.set_aspect('equal')
ax = fig.add_subplot(grid[1, :])
sep = np.arange(len(strata_app)) * RES / 1e6
ax.plot(sep, strata_ref, color=REF2, lw=3, label='per-diagonal r, hicreppy smoothing')
ax.plot(sep, strata_app, color=APP_COLOUR, lw=1.2, label='per-diagonal r, metacooler-run')
placed = []
for value, colour, name in sorted(((pooled['metacooler-run'], APP_COLOUR, 'SCC, metacooler-run'),
                                   (pooled['hicrep'], REF, 'SCC, hicrep'), (pooled['hicreppy'], REF2, 'SCC, hicreppy'))):
    ax.hlines(value, 0, sep.max(), color=colour, lw=1, ls=(0, (4, 3)))
    label_at = max(value, placed[-1] + 0.05) if placed else value
    placed.append(label_at)
    ax.text(sep.max() + 0.1, label_at, f'{name} {value:.2f}', color=INK2, fontsize=8, va='center', ha='left')
ax.set(xlim=(0, sep.max() * 1.3), ylim=(0, 1.02), xlabel='separation (Mb)', ylabel='Pearson r',
       title='d  chr1, G2 vs 60 min: each diagonal, and the pooled SCC')
ax.legend(loc='lower left')
plt.show()
```

**This comparison fails, and the figure says why.** The two references follow each other closely
(r = `{python} TEXT['hr_lin_py_r']` over the `{python} TEXT['hr_n']` values, mean difference
`{python} TEXT['hr_lin_py']`, at most `{python} TEXT['hr_lin_py_max']` apart), while the app's SCC
follows neither (r ≤ `{python} TEXT['hr_app_r']`) and sits on average `{python} TEXT['hr_app_lin']`
above hicrep and `{python} TEXT['hr_app_py']` above hicreppy. Its **per-diagonal** correlations are
the references' (r = `{python} TEXT['hr_strata_r']` between the two curves in d), so the smoothing
and the correlation are right and the difference is in the **pooling**: on chr1 the app pools
diagonals whose correlation is mostly around `{python} TEXT['hr_chr1_mean']` into
`{python} TEXT['hr_chr1_app']`, where hicrep and hicreppy give `{python} TEXT['hr_chr1_refs']`. The
weight each diagonal gets is the cause. `src/analysis/hicrep.ts` weights a diagonal by
`N √(var₁ · var₂)` of the smoothed **counts**, which on raw counts is dominated by the few diagonals
nearest the main one, where the counts are largest and the correlation highest. Both references — and
the original R package — take that variance of the **ranks** (`vstran`: hicrep's `varVstran`,
hicreppy's `vstrans`), which depends on little but the number of positions, so every diagonal counts
about equally. The app's port does not reproduce the reference here; no source was changed for this
notebook.

```{python}
record('Reproducibility (HiCRep)', 'chicken DT40, 7 maps, 100 kb, raw counts',
       f"hicrep {VERSIONS['hicrep']}; hicreppy {VERSIONS['hicreppy']}",
       f"SCC {TEXT['hr_app_lin']} vs hicrep, {TEXT['hr_app_py']} vs hicreppy (the references differ by {TEXT['hr_lin_py']}); "
       f"per-diagonal r agree (r = {TEXT['hr_strata_r']})",
       'Differs: diagonals weighted by count variance, not rank variance',
       apps=['hicrep', 'hicrep-chr1'], refs=['hicrep', 'hicreppy'])
```

## 8 · 3D model (pastis-NB)

**metacooler-run** `reconstruct3d --method nb`: counts drawn from a negative binomial whose mean is
`β · bᵢ · bⱼ · d^−α`, α = 3, with the file's balancing weights as `bᵢ = 1/wᵢ` and zeros taken as
counts. **Reference:** pastis at GitHub `6888ac2`, the code of Varoquaux, Noble & Vert (2023), used
through its own functions: the dispersion as a function of the mean
(`dispersion.compute_mean_variance`, then the paper's `ExponentialDispersion(degree=1)`), a start
from pastis' MDS, then `negative_binomial_structure.estimate_X` with the same α, the same biases and
`use_zero_entries=True`. The map is the yeast G2/M micro-C, coarsened to 10 kb and balanced with
cooler; both use the same beads — the bins the balancer kept that carry a contact.

The app departs from the paper on purpose (SPECS §25.6): the dispersion is a moment estimate per
separation, taken once, and the start is ShRec3D's MDS. And a 3D model has no unique answer — the
fit is not convex, and chromosomes that barely touch can sit anywhere relative to one another. So
the yardstick is pastis against **itself**, from three MDS seeds. The app is run at its default
budget of 150 steps and with room to converge (1,000).

```{python}
P3 = WORK / 'pastis'
Y10 = P3 / 'Yeast_microC_G2M_10kb.cool'
if REDO or not Y10.exists():
    P3.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    cooler.coarsen_cooler(str(YEAST_G2M), str(Y10), factor=10, chunksize=10_000_000)
    cooler.balance_cooler(cooler.Cooler(str(Y10)), store=True)
mr('reconstruct3d', Y10, '--method', 'nb', '--alpha', 3, '--iterations', 1000, out=P3 / 'app-1000',
   name='reconstruct3d-1000', analysis='3D model (pastis-NB)', label='1,000 steps')
mr('reconstruct3d', Y10, '--method', 'nb', '--alpha', 3, out=P3 / 'app-150',
   name='reconstruct3d-150', analysis='3D model (pastis-NB)', label='150 steps, the default')
PASTIS = script('pastis_nb', r'''
    import sys, cooler, numpy as np, pandas as pd
    from pastis import dispersion
    from pastis.optimization import mds, negative_binomial_structure as nbs
    uri, out, seed = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], int(sys.argv[3])
    clr = cooler.Cooler(uri)
    raw = clr.matrix(balance=False)[:].astype(float)
    w = clr.bins()['weight'][:].to_numpy(float)
    keep = np.isfinite(w) & (raw.sum(axis=0) > 0)  # the beads metacooler-run models
    chroms = clr.bins()['chrom'][:].to_numpy()[keep]
    lengths = np.array([np.sum(chroms == c) for c in pd.unique(chroms)])
    counts, bias = raw[np.ix_(keep, keep)], 1 / w[keep]
    bias /= bias.mean()
    _, mean, variance, weights = dispersion.compute_mean_variance(
        counts, lengths, bias=bias)
    fitted = dispersion.ExponentialDispersion(degree=1)
    fitted.fit(mean, variance, sample_weights=weights ** 0.5)
    start = mds.estimate_X(counts / np.outer(bias, bias), alpha=-3., beta=1.,
                           random_state=np.random.RandomState(seed))
    model = nbs.estimate_X(counts, alpha=-3., beta=1., ini=start.flatten(),
                           dispersion=fitted, bias=bias, lengths=lengths,
                           use_zero_entries=True,
                           random_state=np.random.RandomState(seed))
    np.save(out, model.reshape(-1, 3))
''')
for seed in (0, 1, 2):
    reference(f'pastis-seed{seed}', '3D model (pastis-NB)', 'pastis', [PYTHON, PASTIS, Y10, OUT, seed],
              out=P3 / f'pastis-seed{seed}.npy', label=f'seed {seed}', bench=seed == 0)

clr_y = cooler.Cooler(str(Y10))
raw_y = clr_y.matrix(balance=False)[:].astype(float)
w_y = clr_y.bins()['weight'][:].to_numpy(float)
KEEP = np.isfinite(w_y) & (raw_y.sum(axis=0) > 0)
beads = clr_y.bins()[['chrom', 'start']][:][KEEP].reset_index(drop=True)
bead_chrom = beads['chrom'].astype(str).to_numpy()


def app_model(folder):
    bed = pd.read_csv(one(folder, '*.bed3d'), sep='\t', comment='#', header=None,
                      names=['chrom', 'start', 'end', 'x', 'y', 'z'])
    return beads.merge(bed, on=['chrom', 'start'], how='left')[['x', 'y', 'z']].to_numpy(float)


MODELS = {'metacooler-run, 150 steps': app_model(P3 / 'app-150'),
          'metacooler-run, 1,000 steps': app_model(P3 / 'app-1000'),
          **{f'pastis, seed {s}': np.load(P3 / f'pastis-seed{s}.npy') for s in (0, 1, 2)}}
assert all(model.shape == (KEEP.sum(), 3) and np.isfinite(model).all() for model in MODELS.values()), \
    'a bead is missing from a model'
```

```{python}
from scipy.spatial import procrustes
from scipy.spatial.distance import pdist, squareform

same = squareform(np.equal.outer(bead_chrom, bead_chrom).astype(int), checks=False).astype(bool)
dist = {name: pdist(model) for name, model in MODELS.items()}
contacts = squareform(raw_y[np.ix_(KEEP, KEEP)] * np.outer(w_y[KEEP], w_y[KEEP]), checks=False)
seen = contacts > 0


def per_chromosome_disparity(a, b):
    return np.median([procrustes(a[bead_chrom == c], b[bead_chrom == c])[2] for c in pd.unique(bead_chrom)])


rows = []
names_ = list(MODELS)
for i, a in enumerate(names_):
    for b in names_[i + 1:]:
        kind = ('pastis vs pastis' if a.startswith('pastis') and b.startswith('pastis') else
                'metacooler-run vs metacooler-run' if not b.startswith('pastis') else 'metacooler-run vs pastis')
        rows.append({'models': f'{a} / {b}', 'kind': kind,
                     'within chromosomes, Spearman ρ': stats.spearmanr(dist[a][same], dist[b][same])[0],
                     'between chromosomes, Spearman ρ': stats.spearmanr(dist[a][~same], dist[b][~same])[0],
                     'per-chromosome Procrustes disparity': per_chromosome_disparity(MODELS[a], MODELS[b])})
models_table = pd.DataFrame(rows)
fit_table = pd.DataFrame([{'model': name,
                           'fit, all pairs': stats.spearmanr(1 / d[seen], contacts[seen])[0],
                           'fit, within chromosomes': stats.spearmanr(1 / d[seen & same], contacts[seen & same])[0]}
                          for name, d in dist.items()])
display(show(models_table, precision=3))
show(fit_table, precision=3)
```

The fit is the Spearman correlation between `1/d` and the balanced contacts over every pair of beads
the map counted, computed the same way for every model.

```{python}
#| label: fig-pastis
#| fig-cap: "pastis-NB on the yeast G2/M micro-C map at 10 kb (1,128 beads). a, the distances within chromosomes of the app's converged model against pastis' first seed, each divided by its model's median distance between neighbouring beads; b, how alike two models are, within and between chromosomes, for each pair of runs."
kinds = models_table[models_table['kind'] != 'metacooler-run vs metacooler-run']
cross = kinds[kinds['kind'] == 'metacooler-run vs pastis']
selfs = kinds[kinds['kind'] == 'pastis vs pastis']


def spread(frame, column, digits):
    return f"{frame[column].min():.{digits}f}–{frame[column].max():.{digits}f}"


TEXT['p3_intra_cross'] = spread(cross, 'within chromosomes, Spearman ρ', 3)
TEXT['p3_intra_self'] = spread(selfs, 'within chromosomes, Spearman ρ', 3)
TEXT['p3_inter_cross'] = spread(cross, 'between chromosomes, Spearman ρ', 2)
TEXT['p3_inter_self'] = spread(selfs, 'between chromosomes, Spearman ρ', 2)
TEXT['p3_disp_cross'] = spread(cross, 'per-chromosome Procrustes disparity', 3)
TEXT['p3_disp_self'] = spread(selfs, 'per-chromosome Procrustes disparity', 3)
fits = fit_table.set_index('model')['fit, all pairs']
TEXT['p3_fit_app'] = f"{fits['metacooler-run, 1,000 steps']:.3f}"
pastis_fits = fits[[n for n in fits.index if n.startswith('pastis')]]
TEXT['p3_fit_pastis'] = f"{pastis_fits.min():.3f}–{pastis_fits.max():.3f}"
TEXT['p3_default'] = f"{models_table.loc[models_table['kind'] == 'metacooler-run vs metacooler-run', 'within chromosomes, Spearman ρ'].iloc[0]:.3f}"

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4.6), layout='constrained', width_ratios=[1, 1.15])


def scaled(model):
    d = pdist(model)
    step = np.median(np.linalg.norm(np.diff(model, axis=0), axis=1)[bead_chrom[1:] == bead_chrom[:-1]])
    return d / step


agreement(axes[0], scaled(MODELS['pastis, seed 0'])[same], scaled(MODELS['metacooler-run, 1,000 steps'])[same],
          'pastis, seed 0', 'metacooler-run, 1,000 steps', 'a  distances within chromosomes', scale='log')
ax = axes[1]
for col, metric in enumerate(('within chromosomes, Spearman ρ', 'between chromosomes, Spearman ρ')):
    for offset, frame, colour, label in ((-0.12, cross, APP_COLOUR, 'metacooler-run vs pastis'),
                                         (0.12, selfs, REF, 'pastis vs pastis')):
        ax.scatter(np.full(len(frame), col + offset), frame[metric], s=36, color=colour,
                   label=label if col == 0 else None, zorder=3)
ax.set_xticks([0, 1], ['within chromosomes', 'between chromosomes'])
ax.set(xlim=(-0.5, 1.5), ylim=(0, 1.02), ylabel='Spearman ρ of pairwise distances', title='b  how alike two runs are')
ax.legend(loc='lower left')
plt.show()
```

**Within chromosomes the app's model is pastis' model, a little less exactly than pastis is its own**:
the distances correlate at ρ = `{python} TEXT['p3_intra_cross']` with pastis', where pastis from
another seed gives `{python} TEXT['p3_intra_self']`, and each chromosome's shape is further from
pastis' after superposition (disparity `{python} TEXT['p3_disp_cross']`) than pastis' runs are from one
another (`{python} TEXT['p3_disp_self']`) — the deliberate departures in the dispersion and the start.
**Between chromosomes, the app is as close to pastis as pastis is to itself** (ρ =
`{python} TEXT['p3_inter_cross']` against `{python} TEXT['p3_inter_self']`): what the map says about
where one chromosome sits relative to another is little, and no run pins it down. The app's model
fits the contacts at `{python} TEXT['p3_fit_app']`, pastis' at `{python} TEXT['p3_fit_pastis']`. The
default 150 steps and a converged run give nearly the same model (ρ = `{python} TEXT['p3_default']`
within chromosomes).

Five of the eight reproduce their reference: the directionality index, P(s), yapc's candidates and

compartments give the **same eigenvectors**. The 3D model **fits the map as well as pastis'** and has
its shape, a little further from pastis within chromosomes than pastis' own runs are from one another.
Insulation **correlates** with cooltools where the two definitions agree, over complete windows, and
parts from it where they do not, by design. **HiCRep does not reproduce its reference**: its
per-diagonal correlations are the references', and the weights that pool them are not.

R) and yapc's reproducibility test with two replicates (IDR 2.0.3) are held to their references by the

## Time

Every command in the summary that produced a compared result is timed `{python} str(RUNS)` times —
each `metacooler-run` command, and each reference as it ran (for pastis, the first seed; the chr1
HiCRep run behind panel d is not timed, being a diagnosis rather than a result). Each run is a
**fresh process**, started from this notebook exactly as the summary prints it but writing to a
scratch folder, so its time includes starting up: Node loading `metacooler-run`, Python importing a
reference's packages. Two bare start-ups are timed beside them for scale. The runs go **round
robin** — every command once, then every command again — so that whatever else the machine was doing
is spread across all of them rather than landing on one.

**Wall** time is what a reader waits. **CPU** time — user and system, of the process and every
process it started — says how many cores that took. `metacooler-run` computes on one thread.
cooltools' insulation and P(s), and chromosight, were given `{python} str(THREADS)` processes, and
the numerical libraries under every Python reference may spread their linear algebra over several
cores on their own; the *cores busy* column says what each command used.

```{python}
BENCH = WORK / 'benchmark'
ANALYSES = [row['Analysis'] for row in SUMMARY]


def timed(argv, env=None):
    """Wall and CPU seconds of one command, run from work/validation/ as the others were."""
    before = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_CHILDREN)
    start = time.perf_counter()
    run = subprocess.run(argv, capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=WORK, env=env)
    wall = time.perf_counter() - start
    after = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_CHILDREN)
    if run.returncode:
        raise RuntimeError(f'{typed(argv)}\n{run.stderr[-3000:]}')
    return wall, (after.ru_utime - before.ru_utime) + (after.ru_stime - before.ru_stime)


def jobs():
    """What is timed, in the summary's order: each analysis's metacooler-run commands, then its references."""
    out = [dict(name='start-up', analysis='Start-up only', tool='metacooler-run', label='node, bundle loaded',
                argv=lambda scratch: ['node', str(CLI), 'tasks'], env=None),
           dict(name='start-up-python', analysis='Start-up only', tool='python', label='import cooler, cooltools',
                argv=lambda scratch: [PYTHON, '-c', 'import cooler, cooltools'], env=None)]
    for analysis in ANALYSES:
        for name, app in APP.items():
            if app['analysis'] == analysis and app['bench']:
                out.append(dict(name=name, analysis=analysis, tool='metacooler-run', label=app['label'], env=None,
                                argv=lambda scratch, app=app: app['argv'] + ['--out', rel(scratch)]))
        for name, ref in REFS.items():
            if ref['analysis'] == analysis and ref['bench']:
                out.append(dict(name=name, analysis=analysis, tool=ref['tool'], label=ref['label'], env=ref['env'],
                                argv=lambda scratch, ref=ref: [rel(scratch / ref['out'].name) if a == OUT else a
                                                               for a in ref['argv']]))
    return out


def machine():
    cpu = platform.processor()
    if Path('/proc/cpuinfo').exists():
        cpu = next((line.split(':', 1)[1].strip() for line in open('/proc/cpuinfo') if line.startswith('model name')), cpu)
    try:
        memory = f"{os.sysconf('SC_PAGE_SIZE') * os.sysconf('SC_PHYS_PAGES') / 1e9:.0f} GB"
    except (ValueError, OSError):
        memory = '?'
    node = subprocess.run(['node', '--version'], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
    return {'processor': cpu, 'cores': str(os.cpu_count()), 'memory': memory, 'system': platform.platform(),
            'Node': node, 'Python': platform.python_version(), 'measured': time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')}


def benchmark():
    order, rows = jobs(), []
    for run in range(1, RUNS + 1):
        for i, job in enumerate(order):
            scratch = BENCH / 'scratch' / job['name']
            shutil.rmtree(scratch, ignore_errors=True)
            scratch.mkdir(parents=True)
            wall, cpu = timed(job['argv'](scratch), job['env'])
            shutil.rmtree(scratch, ignore_errors=True)
            rows.append({'order': i, 'analysis': job['analysis'], 'tool': job['tool'], 'variant': job['label'],
                         'run': run, 'wall s': wall, 'CPU s': cpu})
    (BENCH / 'machine.json').write_text(json.dumps(machine(), indent=1))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


if REDO_BENCHMARK or not (BENCH / 'times.tsv').exists():
    BENCH.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    benchmark().to_csv(BENCH / 'times.tsv', sep='\t', index=False)
times = pd.read_csv(BENCH / 'times.tsv', sep='\t', keep_default_na=False)
measures(json.loads((BENCH / 'machine.json').read_text()))
```

```{python}
wide = wide.merge(stats_, on=key).sort_values('order')

wide['CPU, mean'] = wide['cpu']
wide['cores busy'] = wide['cpu'] / wide['mean']
run_columns = [f'run {r}' for r in range(1, RUNS + 1)]
show(wide[['analysis', 'tool', 'variant', *run_columns, 'wall, mean ± sd', 'CPU, mean', 'cores busy']],
```

```{python}
TEXT['t_ref'] = f"{theirs['mean'].min():.1f}–{theirs['mean'].max():.0f} s"
TEXT['t_node'] = f"{boot['metacooler-run']:.2f} s"
TEXT['t_python'] = f"{boot['python']:.1f} s"
TEXT['t_cores_app'] = f"{(mine['cpu'] / mine['mean']).max():.1f}"

TEXT['t_sd'] = f"{(timed_['sd'] / timed_['mean']).max():.0%}"
```

Times are in seconds; *cores busy* is the mean CPU time over the mean wall time. Every
`metacooler-run` command here takes `{python} TEXT['t_app']`, and every reference
`{python} TEXT['t_ref']`. Of that, starting Node with the bundle takes `{python} TEXT['t_node']` and
importing cooler and cooltools `{python} TEXT['t_python']`. `metacooler-run` never keeps more than
`{python} TEXT['t_cores_app']` cores busy — its one thread, and Node's own housekeeping — where a
reference keeps up to `{python} TEXT['t_cores_ref']`. Across its runs, no analysis command's time
spreads by more than `{python} TEXT['t_sd']` of its mean (sd over mean).
